content:
Hello all,
I hope you are well!
My name is Idan, and I am working with my collaborators at Case Western Reserve University to create a Lean Benchmark for graduate-level stochastic-processes questions. We are new to the Mathlib infrastructure, and looking to some suggestions for the following:
Running our natural language questions through some prominent formalizer models with Mathlib search, it becomes evident that ~40% of them cannot be represented given the current Mathlib infrastructure (Poisson process, continuous-time Markov chains, mixing/hitting/cover times, etc), prompting the models to return abstractions of various degrees which we are unable to use for benchmarking purposes.
I would greatly appreciate your insight on how to proceed, whether a specific individual is already working on expanding that section of Mathlib, whether that's an avenue for us to pursue, or any general information you think would be valuable for us moving forward.
Thank you for your time!
In gratitude,
Idan Davidovich.

A stochastic process is basically a collection X:(t:T)→Ω→XX : (t : T) \to \Omega \to \mathcal{X}X:(t:T)→Ω→X such that each X t is docs#AEMeasurable. There are some related general concepts: MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime, MeasureTheory.hittingBtwn, MeasureTheory.stoppedValue, MeasureTheory.stoppedProcess, MeasureTheory.Martingale... There are many things being developed in the #Brownian motion project.

Regarding concrete constructions, in Mathlib I am only aware of ProbabilityTheory.IsPreBrownianReal. There isn't a general definition of Markov processes (though some people are thinking about it), Markov chains, random walks etc. in Mathlib.
